SELECTED_INDEX: 9
CONFIDENCE: 0.25
EXPLANATION: Three bands in the triple-bond region are observed: very strong peaks at 2151 cm⁻¹ and 2171 cm⁻¹ together with a weaker one at 2255 cm⁻¹.  
• A C≡N (nitrile) stretch normally appears near 2240–2260 cm⁻¹ and fits the 2255 cm⁻¹ line.  
• Azide groups (–N₃) show intense asymmetric ν(N₃) stretches in the 2100–2170 cm⁻¹ range, matching the pair at 2151/2171 cm⁻¹.  
Candidate 9 ([N#CNN(N=[N+]=[N-])N=[N+]=[N-]) contains one nitrile and multiple azide groups, uniquely accounting for all three triple-bond peaks among the listed structures.  
Lower-frequency features (∼540, 611, 678 cm⁻¹) correspond to bending modes of the azide unit, while the 869 and 904 cm⁻¹ bands can be assigned to coupled N–N stretches/rocking motions often seen for polyazides. No other candidate simultaneously supplies both a nitrile and azide functionality, so candidate 9 best matches the experimental Raman spectrum.
